{"id":116,"title":"multiplayer sync issue","body":"
## Problem statement

Panopt works correctly in a single Zellij client, but when two clients attach to the same Zellij session, **plugin panes diverge between clients**.

Plain terminal panes behave as expected: both clients see the same PTY output. The divergence only happens in panes running a Panopt/Zellij plugin.

This indicates that the plugin’s visible state is being held inside a **client-local plugin instance**, rather than being derived from a **shared session-level state model**.

## Reproduction

1. Start Panopt in a named Zellij session.

   ```sh
   zellij attach --create panopt
   ```

2. From another terminal or machine, attach a second client to the same session.

   ```sh
   zellij attach panopt
   ```

3. In a normal terminal pane, type something.

   Expected: both clients see the same output.

4. In a Panopt plugin pane, change a visible value, mode, form field, selection, or pane content.

   Actual: the second client sees the change locally, but the first client does not.

## Expected behavior

All committed Panopt state should be shared across clients attached to the same Zellij session.

Examples of shared state:

```text
current view/mode
form field values
selected entity/task
pane role/assignment
command state
document/model contents
```

Client-local state is fine for transient UI details:

```text
cursor position
focus
scroll offset
selection
half-typed uncommitted input
hover/highlight state
```

## Likely root cause

Each attached Zellij client gets its own plugin instance or plugin render state. The plugin is treating its in-memory state as authoritative.

That works for one client, but fails with multiple attached clients because each plugin instance mutates only its own local state.

Current broken model:

```text
client A -> plugin instance A -> local state A
client B -> plugin instance B -> local state B
```

Needed model:

```text
client A -> plugin instance A ┐
                              ├-> shared Panopt state -> broadcast/update -> all plugin instances repaint
client B -> plugin instance B ┘
```

## Fix direction

Move authoritative Panopt state out of the plugin instance.

The plugin should be a **view/controller**, not the state owner.

Use a shared session-scoped backend, for example:

```text
single panoptd process per Zellij session
Unix socket
SQLite database
state file + file watcher
local event bus
Zellij plugin pipes, if suitable
```

On every committed change:

```text
plugin receives input
plugin sends mutation to shared state owner
state owner applies mutation
state owner increments generation/version
all plugin instances are notified or poll
all plugin instances reload state
all plugin panes repaint from the same snapshot
```

## Useful diagnostic instrumentation

Add this to every plugin pane:

```text
zellij session: <name>
plugin instance id: <uuid>
state backend: <path/socket/db>
state generation: <number>
last update source: <client/plugin id>
```

Then attach two clients. If changing a value increments the generation only in one plugin pane, state is still local. If both panes show the same generation and state snapshot, synchronization is working.

## One-sentence version

“Panopt plugin panes are not multiplayer-safe: terminal panes share PTY state correctly, but plugin panes keep authoritative UI/application state inside per-client plugin instances, so attached clients diverge; fix by moving committed state to a session-scoped shared state backend and making plugins render from that state.”

Perfect! Now I have a comprehensive understanding. Let me create a summary document based on my findings:

## Summary: Panopt Zellij Plugin Architecture & Multiplayer Sync Bug

I've thoroughly analyzed the plugin crate at `/home/gregz/cp/panopt/crates/panopt-zellij/src/main.rs`. Here are the core findings:

### 1. Overall Architecture

**Entry Point & Registration:**
- Lines 622: `register_plugin!(PanoptPane);` — the macro generates `main` and binds the Zellij plugin interface
- Lines 624-905: `impl ZellijPlugin for PanoptPane` — implements the trait with `load()`, `update()`, `pipe()`, and `render()` methods

**Plugin Structure:**
- Five independent plugin instances run in parallel (one per `Mode`): Todos, Agents, Terminals, Commands, Notes
- Each instance is identified by `(plugin_url, mode=<kind>)` and can be addressed individually via `zellij action pipe --plugin-configuration "mode=<kind>"`
- Zellij distributes events (`PaneUpdate`, `Timer`, `Key`, `Mouse`, `PermissionRequestResult`) to all instances

### 2. In-Memory State (`PanoptPane` struct, lines 390-553)

**Authoritative Application/View State:**
- **`todos: Vec<(u64, String)>`** — parsed todos from `.panopt/todos.md` (line 412)
- **`notes: Vec<(u64, String)>`** — parsed notes from `.panopt/notes.md` (line 414)
- **`processes: Vec<ProcessRow>`** — parsed processes from `.panopt/processes.md` (line 419)
- **`panes: Vec<PaneRow>`** — live panes flattened from Zellij's `PaneManifest` (line 421)
- **`agent_labels: BTreeMap<u32, String>`** — sidebar labels for agent panes, written to shared file `/host/.panopt/.cockpit/agent-labels.json` (lines 479-484)
- **`agent_pane_ids: BTreeMap<u32, String>`** — stable daemon agent IDs per terminal pane (lines 486-493)
- **`slot_pane: Option<PaneId>`** — the designated content slot target (lines 459-463)
- **`todo_filter: TodoFilter`** — current filter (line 430)
- **`todo_sort_1 / todo_sort_2: TodoSort`** — sort axes (lines 434, 439)

**Transient UI State (not persisted):**
- **`cursor: usize`** — keyboard-selected item index (line 442)
- **`scroll: usize`** — topmost rendered item (line 445)
- **`last_rows / last_cols: usize`** — cached render dimensions (lines 448, 454)
- **`show_help: bool`** — help overlay toggle (line 540)
- **`sidebar_focused: bool`** — whether sidebar has keyboard focus (line 502)
- **`focused_is_floating: bool`** — whether focused pane is floating (line 510)
- **`plugin_pane / search_pane`** — pane IDs (lines 458, 468)
- **`last_frame_title / last_pane_titles`** — cached titles to suppress redundant host calls (lines 524, 529)

**Data-Derived State:**
- **`items: Vec<Item>`** — rebuilt on every change from `todos`, `notes`, `processes`, and `panes` (line 425)

### 3. Data Loading from panoptd

**Mechanism:** File polling via 1-second timer, NOT HTTP or daemon polling.

**Code flow:**
1. **Initial load (line 675 in `load()`):** `self.reload_data()` — reads projection files once on startup
2. **1-second timer (line 678):** `set_timeout(1.0)` — subscribes to `EventType::Timer`
3. **Timer handler (lines 694-723 in `update()`):**
   ```rust
   Event::Timer(_) => {
       self.reload_data();      // Line 712 - re-read projection files every second
       self.rebuild_items();
       self.sync_pane_titles();
       set_timeout(1.0);        // Line 721 - re-arm timer
       true
   }
   ```

**`reload_data()` (lines 1131-1153):** Reads from disk based on mode:
```rust
fn reload_data(&mut self) {
    match self.mode {
        Mode::Todos => {
            self.todos = read_index("/host/.panopt/todos.md");
            self.notes = read_index("/host/.panopt/notes.md");
            self.processes = read_processes("/host/.panopt/processes.md");
            self.read_agent_labels();
        }
        Mode::Notes => {
            self.notes = read_index("/host/.panopt/notes.md");
        }
        Mode::Agents | Mode::Commands => {
            self.processes = read_processes("/host/.panopt/processes.md");
            self.read_agent_labels();
        }
        Mode::Terminals => {
            self.read_agent_labels();
        }
    }
}
```

**Other data refresh triggers:**
- **`Event::PaneUpdate(manifest)`** (line 687): Zellij pane manifest changes → `ingest_panes()` → `rebuild_items()` (no file re-read)

### 4. Render & Update Cycle

**Rendering:**
- `render(rows, cols)` (lines 832-904) — called by Zellij when the pane needs redraw
  - Clears body rows, renders `self.items` with ANSI cursor positioning
  - No file I/O, no data fetching
  - Caches `last_rows` / `last_cols` for title fitting

**Update events subscription (lines 668-674):**
```rust
subscribe(&[
    EventType::PaneUpdate,    // Zellij pane manifest changed
    EventType::Key,           // User keyboard input
    EventType::Mouse,         // User mouse input
    EventType::Timer,         // 1-second tick
    EventType::PermissionRequestResult,
]);
```

**Update cycle:**
- `update(event)` (lines 681-736) returns `bool` (dirty flag)
- Only `Timer`, `PaneUpdate`, `Key`, `Mouse` cause updates
- No continuous polling or background threads

### 5. Mutations: Writing State Back

**Mutations are written to disk, NOT back to panoptd daemon via HTTP:**

**File-based coordination:**
1. **Agent labels projection (line 1367, 2218):** 
   ```rust
   write_agent_labels(&self.agent_labels);  // Todos pane writes to /host/.panopt/.cockpit/agent-labels.json
   ```
   Other panes read it via `read_agent_labels()` (lines 1375-1382)

2. **Viewer routing files (lines 2074, 2089, 2096):**
   ```rust
   write_routing(kind, id, &slot_name);  // Writes /host/.panopt/.cockpit/viewer-<slot>.json
   ```
   Tells `panopt _viewer` what to display

3. **Content pane count (line 2464):**
   ```rust
   write_content_count(count);  // Writes /host/.panopt/.cockpit/content-count
   ```
   For viewers to know if they're the last pane

4. **Destructive CLI calls (lines 2024-2029, 1969-1985):**
   ```rust
   fn run_panopt(&self, args: &[&str], cwd: PathBuf) {
       run_command_with_env_variables_and_cwd(&full, ...);  // Spawns panopt CLI
   }
   // e.g., self.run_panopt(&["todo", "rm", &id.to_string(), "--port", &self.port], cwd);
   ```
   Deletes are delegated to the CLI, not done in-memory

**No daemon API calls:** All mutations → file writes or CLI invocation → file system side effects

### 6. Generation/Version Numbers & Polling

**No explicit generation numbers or versioning:**
- Projection files (`.panopt/todos.md`, etc.) are the source of truth
- Plugin re-reads them every 1 second unconditionally
- Routing files (`.cockpit/viewer-<slot>.json`) are JSON blobs written atomically (temp + rename)

**Polling mechanism:**
```rust
// line 678 in load()
set_timeout(1.0);

// lines 721 in update() Timer arm
set_timeout(1.0);
```
Zellij's `set_timeout()` API requests another `Timer` event in N seconds.

### **ROOT CAUSE OF MULTIPLAYER SYNC BUG**

Each plugin instance has **completely independent in-memory state**:
- When Client A's Todos pane reads `todos.md` at time T1, it caches into `self.todos`
- When Client B's Todos pane reads `todos.md` at time T1+0.1, it gets the same snapshot but into its own `self.todos`
- If Client A's form autosave writes a mutation to `todos.md` at T1+0.5, Client B's pane won't see it until its next timer tick at T1+1.0
- **Critical:** Each Zellij session is a separate OS process with its own plugin WASM instances — they do NOT share memory

The five sidebar panes diverge because:
1. Each pane instance (Todos, Agents, Terminals, Commands, Notes) is independent
2. Each Zellij client session runs its own plugin instances
3. File-based coordination (`agent-labels.json`, routing files) only works for simple flags, not complex state
4. **No inter-client synchronization mechanism** — the 1-second poll reads local filesystem, not a shared daemon state

**Key File Paths for Synchronization:**
- `/host/.panopt/todos.md` — source of truth, polled every 1 second
- `/host/.panopt/notes.md`
- `/host/.panopt/processes.md`
- `/host/.panopt/.cockpit/agent-labels.json` — only Todos writes, others read
- `/host/.panopt/.cockpit/viewer-<slot>.json` — routing per viewer instance
- `/host/.panopt/.cockpit/content-count` — only Todos writes

# Implementation Plan — Todo #116 "multiplayer sync issue"

## Headline finding (the honest framing)

The todo's premise — "plugin keeps authoritative state in per-client instances" — is **mostly already false** for panopt. Committed state (todos, notes, processes, locks, agents) lives in SQLite in panoptd and is projected atomically to `.panopt/*.md`. Both clients' plugin instances poll those same files every 1 s via `reload_data()` (main.rs:1131) on `Event::Timer` (main.rs:694). So "current view contents / form values / document model / task list" are **already shared**.

A second decisive fact I verified in the zellij-tile 0.44.3 API: `PluginIds` (zellij-utils `data.rs:2701`) carries `plugin_id`, `zellij_pid`, `initial_cwd`, and **`client_id: ClientId` (= `u16`)**. In Zellij's tiled-plugin model a plugin pane is **one instance whose render is broadcast to all attached clients** — there is not a separate `PanoptPane` struct per client. `get_plugin_ids().client_id` returns the client that triggered the *current* command, not a per-instance identity. This means the "client A → instance A → local state A" divergence model in the report does **not** apply to panopt's tiled sidebar panes the way it would to a naive plugin.

Therefore the plan is deliberately staged: **instrument first, prove the model, then do only the small hardening that's actually warranted** (gatekeeper races + refresh latency), NOT a "move state out of the plugin" refactor that is already done.

---

## Increment 1 (recommended minimal first step): Diagnostic footer, gated by `debug=1`

Goal: ship the five-field overlay the todo asks for, off by default, so two clients can be attached and the generation observed. Pure plugin-side change; no daemon/core changes; one WASM crate.

### 1a. Add fields to `PanoptPane` (main.rs:390-553)
- `debug: bool` — set in `load()` from config key `debug` (`configuration.get("debug").map(|v| v == "1" || v == "true").unwrap_or(false)`), same pattern as the existing `mode`/`ws`/`port` reads at main.rs:640-648.
- `session_name: Option<String>` — populated from `ModeInfo.session_name`.
- `client_id: u16`, `plugin_id: u32` — cached from `get_plugin_ids()` in `load()` (already partially done at main.rs:654, which calls `get_plugin_ids()` for `plugin_pane`; reuse that one call, bind the whole struct to a local and read `.client_id`/`.plugin_id`/`.plugin_id`).
- `state_generation: u64`, `last_update_source: Option<String>` — read from the generation file (Increment 2) or, in this increment, derived from max mtime (see 1c fallback).

### 1b. Session name source
The plugin currently does **not** subscribe to `EventType::ModeUpdate`. Add it to the `subscribe(&[...])` list at main.rs:668-674, and add an `Event::ModeUpdate(mode_info)` arm in `update()` (main.rs:681) that stores `mode_info.session_name`. `ModeInfo.session_name` is `Option<String>` (verified, data.rs:1730). This is the only first-class API for the session name; `get_session_environment_variables()` exists but does not reliably carry the session name. Subscribing to `ModeUpdate` is cheap and idempotent with the existing render gating.

### 1c. State generation — derive from max mtime in this increment (no daemon dependency)
For the minimal first increment, compute generation as the **max mtime (as unix millis) across the projection files this mode reads** — reuse the exact paths already in `reload_data()` (main.rs:1131): `todos.md`, `notes.md`, `processes.md`, plus `.cockpit/agent-labels.json`. Add a helper `fn projection_generation() -> u64` next to `read_index` (main.rs:2791) using `fs::metadata(path).modified()`. This needs no panoptd or core change and is enough to answer the todo's core question ("does the generation move in both panes when one client mutates?"). `last_update_source` is **not cheaply derivable from mtime** — show it as `-` (n/a) in this increment and defer the real value to Increment 2's generation file.

### 1d. Render the footer (`render`, main.rs:832)
When `self.debug`, reserve the **bottom body row** (one extra row, the same pattern the Todos status line already uses at main.rs:894-903) and print a dim one-liner:
```
sess:<name> cl:<client_id> pid:<plugin_id> gen:<n> src:<source> be:.panopt
```
Reuse the existing `paint(..., Style::Dim, false)` helper and absolute cursor positioning (`\x1b[{row};1H\x1b[2K`) already used throughout `render`. Subtract one from the item-area row budget when `debug` is on (adjust `list_rows()` or the local `body_rows` math) so the footer never overlaps the list. Keep it on every mode's pane, not just Todos.

### 1e. Build / verify
- `cargo check --manifest-path crates/panopt-zellij/Cargo.toml --target wasm32-wasip1`
- `cargo clippy --manifest-path crates/panopt-zellij/Cargo.toml --target wasm32-wasip1` (`-D warnings`)
- `just plugin-release` for the artifact, or the `verify-all` skill for the dual-target sweep.
- The layout must pass `debug "1"` in the plugin config block to turn it on; default off.

**Why this is the right first cut:** it is read-only w.r.t. shared state, touches one excluded WASM crate, respects every invariant (no pane closing, no projection writes, no tool-surface change), and directly produces the evidence the todo demands.

---

## Increment 2: Real generation counter + `last update source` (daemon-backed) — only if Increment 1 shows mtime is too coarse

mtime works but is coarse (second/millisecond granularity, and re-projection of unchanged files can bump it). A clean monotonic counter is better and carries the update source.

### 2a. panopt-core: a single choke point for the bump
There is **no existing single choke point** — `state.rs` has ~7 scattered `reproject_*` helpers (`reproject_todos` 1467, `reproject_notes_index` 1479, `reproject_note_full` 1489, `reproject_agent_tools` 1513, `reproject_processes` 1519, `reproject_agents` 1525, `reproject_locks` 1535) plus `reproject_all` (1543), and the daemon's `handler.rs` has ~30 separate `state.lock()` sites. Do **not** instrument the handler. Instead:

- Add `fn bump_generation(&self, project: ProjectId, source: &str) -> Result<(), CoreError>` on `Store` in `state.rs`, next to `project_root` (state.rs:1454). It increments a per-project counter (new column `projects.generation INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` via a **forward-only** `V<n>` migration block in `db.rs` per the invariant) and writes a tiny projection file.
- Add `projection::project_generation(root: &Path, gen: u64, source: &str)` in `projection.rs` next to the other `project_*` fns (projection.rs:451 region), using the existing `atomic_write` (projection.rs:85) — temp+rename, honoring the atomic-projection invariant. Target file: `.panopt/.cockpit/generation` with body like `<n>\n<source>\n`. (`.cockpit/` is the right home — it's the cockpit's non-human routing dir, already git-ignored via the `*` `.gitignore` from `bootstrap`.)
- Call `bump_generation` from each `reproject_*` helper's tail (they already each resolve `project_root`, so the cost is one extra atomic write). Cleaner alternative: wrap the public mutators. Given the scatter, the **lowest-risk** placement is one `self.bump_generation(project, source)?` at the end of each `reproject_*` helper, since every mutation funnels through exactly one of them. `source` is the agent/connection identity already available in the handler — thread it down as a `&str` param, or default to a coarse `"daemon"` if threading the caller id is too invasive for a first pass.

### 2b. plugin: read the generation file
In `reload_data()` (main.rs:1131), after the existing index reads, read `/host/.panopt/.cockpit/generation`, parse line 1 → `state_generation`, line 2 → `last_update_source`. Add a `read_generation()` helper near `read_index` (main.rs:2791). Tolerant parse (missing file → `gen:0 src:-`), matching the `read_agent_labels` tolerance style.

### 2c. Build/verify
Workspace side (`db.rs`, `state.rs`, `projection.rs`, `handler.rs`) builds for host: `cargo check -p panopt-core -p panoptd`, `cargo clippy -p panopt-core -p panoptd`. Plugin side as in 1e. Daemon must be restarted to pick up new daemon code: `just stop && just up` (per CLAUDE.md daemon lifecycle).

**Decision — mtime vs counter:** Recommend shipping **mtime in Increment 1** (zero daemon risk, answers the diagnostic question) and only promoting to the **daemon counter in Increment 2** if you want `last update source` and a clean monotonic value. The counter is the cleaner long-term answer; mtime is the cheaper proof-of-concept.

---

## Increment 3: Confirm-or-refute interpretation (what the footer proves)

Concrete reading guide to write into the todo/HANDOFF as the result:

- **Attach two clients** to one session (`zellij attach --create panopt`, then `zellij attach panopt` from a second terminal). Both render the *same* tiled sidebar — in Zellij a tiled plugin is one instance broadcast to all clients, so by construction both clients show the identical footer.
- **Mutate committed state** from client B (create a todo, change a process). Expected: within ≤1 s **both** panes show the same incremented `gen:` and the same list — because both poll the same projection files. This **refutes** the "state is local" hypothesis for committed state.
- **Mutate transient UI** (move cursor / scroll / toggle `?` help / cycle filter) in client B. Expected: this is genuinely client-local in the report's intended sense — BUT because Zellij broadcasts one render, both clients actually see it. If the user perceives divergence here, the real cause is Zellij's per-client input focus, not panopt state. The footer's `cl:` field (different `client_id` per triggering client) makes this visible.
- **Conclusion the plan commits to:** the "fix" reduces to (a) gatekeeper-race hardening and (b) refresh-latency tightening — **not** a state-ownership refactor. State the plan will say so explicitly.

---

When in multiplayer mode, each client launches a plugin instance. This is an important architectural aspect of how Zellij handles plugins in shared sessions.

WASM plugins often maintain multiple Grid instances (one per ClientId) to allow different clients to see different plugin states. Additionally, the server maintains separate state for each connected client: each client receives customized render output based on their terminal size and active pane.

## Pipe Communication in Multiplayer Sessions

That settles the mechanism. The web sources confirm it: **in multiplayer, each attached client launches its own plugin WASM instance with its own `thread_local` `STATE`** — independent state and independent rendering per client. That's exactly why panopt's sidebar diverges: each client's plugin instance has its own `cursor`/`scroll`/`todo_filter`/`todo_sort`/`show_help`, and nothing shares them. (The *data* — `todos`/`notes`/`processes` — already converges because every instance polls the same `.panopt/*.md` files; the view state never converges because it lives only in instance memory.) Crucially, the sources also confirm **pipes are delivered to every instance of a plugin across clients** — panopt's existing synchronization primitive.

So the fix is bounded: externalize the *view/presentation* state to a shared session-scoped store all instances read, and nudge them to repaint together. Let me get concrete placement with the corrected framing.

## Verified problem framing (this is the corrected understanding — earlier framing about SQLite/todo data was WRONG)

The bug is about **Zellij plugin PRESENTATION diverging across attached clients**, not about panopt todo/note data.

Verified facts:
- In Zellij multiplayer (v0.44.3, zellij-tile 0.44.3), **each attached client launches its OWN plugin WASM instance** with its own `thread_local!` `STATE` (RefCell<PanoptPane>). Confirmed via zellij-tile `register_plugin!` (STATE is thread_local) and Zellij docs ("each client launches a plugin instance"; "WASM plugins maintain multiple Grid instances, one per ClientId").
- Therefore each client's `PanoptPane` instance has independent in-memory state and renders independently.
- panopt runs 5 instances PER CLIENT — one per `Mode` (Todos/Agents/Terminals/Commands/Notes), set from the `mode` plugin-config key in `load()` (main.rs:625).
- DATA already converges across clients: `todos`/`notes`/`processes` are read from `.panopt/*.md` files (projected by panoptd) every 1s via `reload_data()` (main.rs:1131) on `Event::Timer` (set_timeout(1.0), main.rs:678/721). All instances poll the same files, so the lists match within ~1s.
- VIEW state does NOT converge — it lives only in instance memory and is never shared. The user wants the sidebar to behave like a shared terminal pane: **all clients see an IDENTICAL, synchronized presentation** (if one client's view changes, every client's view changes).

The per-instance view/presentation fields in `PanoptPane` (main.rs:390-553) that drive `render()` and must be synchronized to make every client identical:
- `cursor: usize` (selected row), `scroll: usize` (top visible row)
- `todo_filter: TodoFilter` (cycled with f/F), `todo_sort_1`/`todo_sort_2: TodoSort` (cycled 1/!,2/@)
- `show_help: bool` (toggled by ?)
These are per-mode-pane (Todos cursor is independent of Notes cursor), so synchronization must be scoped per Mode: client A's Todos instance must share with client B's Todos instance, but not with the Notes instances.

## Synchronization primitives ALREADY in the codebase (reuse these)
- **Shared `.cockpit/` files**: panopt already writes/reads JSON in `/host/.panopt/.cockpit/` for cross-instance coordination — e.g. `agent-labels.json` (write_agent_labels/read_agent_labels ~main.rs:1367/1375), `viewer-<slot>.json` (write_routing), `content-count`. These are read by all instances on the 1s timer. This is the established "shared session-scoped state" channel.
- **Atomic write** pattern (temp + rename) is used for these files — match it.
- **Pipes reach ALL instances across clients**: the `pipe()` method (main.rs:743) handles `zellij action pipe` messages; Zellij delivers a pipe directed at a plugin to every instance of it (confirmed in Zellij plugin-pipes docs). panopt already narrows delivery with `--plugin-configuration "mode=todos"`. A pipe NOT narrowed by client reaches every client's matching instance — this is the way to force all instances to repaint immediately.
- `reload_data()` is the natural place to also load shared view state each tick.

## What to design

1. **Shared view-state store**: a per-mode JSON file under `.cockpit/` (e.g. `.cockpit/view-<mode-letter>.json`, reusing `Mode::letter` already used for slot-name allocation) holding `{cursor, scroll, filter, sort_1, sort_2, show_help, seq}` where `seq` is a monotonic counter for last-writer-wins. Specify the struct, the read/write helpers (next to the existing `read_agent_labels`/`write_agent_labels` and `read_index`), and atomic write.

2. **Write-on-change**: in the Key/Mouse handlers (`handle_key` ~main.rs and `handle_mouse`) that mutate cursor/scroll/filter/sort/show_help, after the mutation, the acting instance writes the shared file with seq+1. Identify exactly which handler sites mutate these fields (cursor movement j/k/arrows, page scroll, f/F filter, 1/!/2/@ sort, ? help) and where to hook the write so it's one choke point if possible (e.g. a `persist_view()` called at the end of `update()` when dirty AND the change was a view change). Consider: should EVERY dirty update persist, or only view-affecting ones? Recommend the simplest correct choke point.

3. **Read-and-adopt**: in `reload_data()` (or a sibling called from the same Timer arm), each instance reads its mode's view file; if `seq` is newer than the last seq it applied, adopt cursor/scroll/filter/sort/show_help into self and mark dirty so the next render repaints. Must avoid a write/read feedback loop: an instance writes only on local input, reads only adopts when seq is strictly newer than what it last wrote/applied. Specify how to track `last_applied_seq` and how the acting instance avoids re-adopting its own write.

4. **Instant propagation (optional but recommended)**: after writing, broadcast a pipe (e.g. name `panopt:view-sync`, narrowed to the same `mode=<letter>` so only same-mode instances react) so other clients' instances reload the view file and repaint immediately rather than waiting up to 1s for their timer. Specify how panopt sends a pipe from inside the plugin (does it shell out via `zellij action pipe`, like its other pipe emissions? find the existing emit path) and how `pipe()` should handle the new message (call the read-and-adopt + return true to repaint). If sending a self-pipe is awkward from WASM, note that the 1s timer fallback already converges and the pipe is just latency polish.

5. **Edge cases**: cursor must stay in `0..items.len()` after adopting (clamp, reusing existing clamp logic); a client whose item list briefly differs (mid-poll) should clamp not panic; show_help is global per the design; seq overflow is irrelevant (u64). Also: the boot cleanup `fs::remove_dir_all("/host/.panopt/.cockpit")` runs only in the Todos instance at load (main.rs:660) — ensure view files live under `.cockpit/` so they get cleared on a fresh cockpit boot (correct) but are NOT clobbered mid-session.

6. **Scope check & alternatives**: briefly state whether a smaller subset (sync only cursor+scroll+filter+sort, treat show_help as local) would satisfy "identical presentation", and recommend. Also note the known remaining multiplayer hazard NOT in scope: two per-client Todos "gatekeeper" instances both driving content-pane swaps/preview from a now-shared cursor — call this out as a follow-up risk but keep the core plan to presentation sync.

Give the WASM build/clippy commands and a two-client verification recipe. Recommend a minimal first increment.

# Plan — todo #116: synchronize Zellij sidebar presentation across attached clients

## Context

**Problem.** When two clients attach to the same Zellij session, the panopt sidebar
*plugin panes diverge*: a view change made in one client (move the selection, change
filter/sort) is not reflected in the other client's pane. The desired behavior (chosen by
the user) is **identical/synchronized** — the sidebar should behave like a shared terminal
pane: if one client's view changes, every client's view changes too.

**Root cause (verified).** In Zellij multiplayer (v0.44.3 / zellij-tile 0.44.3) **each
attached client launches its own plugin WASM instance** with its own `thread_local!` `STATE`
(`RefCell<PanoptPane>`) — confirmed in `zellij-tile`'s `register_plugin!` and in Zellij docs
("each client launches a plugin instance"; "WASM plugins maintain one Grid per ClientId").
panopt runs **5 instances per client**, one per `Mode` (Todos/Agents/Terminals/Commands/Notes).

- The *data* (`todos`/`notes`/`processes`) **already converges** across clients: every
  instance polls the same `.panopt/*.md` files every 1s in `reload_data()`
  (`main.rs:1131`, called from the `Event::Timer` arm at `main.rs:712`).
- The *view state* (`cursor`, `scroll`, `todo_filter`, `todo_sort_1/2`, `show_help`) lives
  **only in instance memory** and is never shared, so it never converges. **That is the bug.**

This is **not** about panopt todo/note data sync (an earlier misframing). The fix is bounded:
externalize the per-mode *view* state to the shared session-scoped channel panopt already
uses (`/host/.panopt/.cockpit/*.json`, atomic temp+rename, polled on the 1s timer), and
optionally nudge instances to repaint immediately via a broadcast pipe.

All changes are in **`crates/panopt-zellij/src/main.rs`** (the WASM plugin crate, excluded
from the workspace, built only for `wasm32-wasip1`). No daemon, core, or MCP-tool changes.

## Approach

Per-`Mode` shared view-state file with a monotonic `seq` (last-writer-wins). The acting
instance writes on local input; all instances read-and-adopt on the timer (and, optionally,
on a broadcast pipe for instant propagation). Reuse the existing `.cockpit/` write/read
idiom, `Mode::letter()`/`slug()`, the `clamp_cursor()` path, and the `run_command([…,"pipe",…])`
emit pattern.

### 1. Shared view-state store
- New struct near `ProcessRow` (~`main.rs:555`):
  `ViewState { cursor, scroll, filter: TodoFilter, sort_1, sort_2: TodoSort, show_help: bool, seq: u64 }`.
- Per-mode path keyed by `Mode::letter()` (already used for slot allocation, `main.rs:103`):
  `.cockpit/view-<letter>.json` (e.g. `view-t.json` for Todos). Per-mode keying is required —
  Todos cursor is independent of Notes cursor; only same-mode instances across clients share.
- `write_view_state(mode, &ViewState)` next to `write_agent_labels` — hand-rolled serializer
  + temp-then-`rename` (match `write_agent_labels`/`write_routing`; no JSON dep). Add stable
  integer wire codes `to_wire`/`from_wire` on `TodoFilter` and `TodoSort`.
- `read_view_state(mode) -> Option<ViewState>` next to `read_agent_labels` — tolerant parse
  (missing/partial file → `None`; unknown filter/sort code → keep current), mirroring
  `parse_agent_labels`.
- Add two `PanoptPane` fields near the view fields (~`main.rs:440`): `view_seq: u64`,
  `last_applied_seq: u64` (default 0).

### 2. Write-on-change (single choke point)
- In `update()` (`main.rs:681`), for the **`Event::Key` and `Event::Mouse` arms only**
  (the only events expressing local view intent), snapshot a `view_fingerprint()` tuple
  before dispatch and compare after; if it changed, call `bump_and_persist_view()`.
- `bump_and_persist_view()`: `view_seq += 1`; set `last_applied_seq = view_seq` (so we never
  re-adopt our own write); `write_view_state(self.mode, …)`; then `broadcast_view_sync()` (§4).
- Do **not** persist on `Timer`/`PaneUpdate`: those re-run `rebuild_items()`/`clamp_cursor()`
  which can legitimately move `cursor`/`scroll` as the list changes — a local clamp, not user
  intent, and every instance clamps identically against the same projection. Persisting there
  would race seq numbers and clobber another client's newer write.

### 3. Read-and-adopt (no feedback loop)
- `adopt_view_state()` called at the end of `reload_data()` (`main.rs:1131`):
  read the mode's file; if `v.seq <= self.last_applied_seq` return (skips our own write and
  stale seqs); else adopt all fields, set `view_seq = v.seq`, `last_applied_seq = v.seq`.
- The Timer arm already calls `reload_data()` then `rebuild_items()` → `clamp_cursor()`
  (`main.rs:1510`), so the adopted cursor/scroll are clamped against this instance's current
  items automatically — handles mid-poll list divergence with no new clamp code and no panic
  on empty/short lists. `load()` also runs `reload_data()` before `rebuild_items()`, so a
  late-joining client adopts the current shared view on boot.

### 4. Instant propagation (recommended; latency polish only)
- After a write, `broadcast_view_sync()` shells out via `run_command([…,"action","pipe",
  "--name","panopt:view-sync","--plugin-configuration",&format!("mode={}",self.mode.slug()),
  "--",&self.view_seq.to_string()])` — same pattern as `request_focus_pane` (`main.rs:1877`).
- Handle `"panopt:view-sync"` in `pipe()` (`main.rs:743`) in the early mode-agnostic block
  (before the `if self.mode != Mode::Todos` guard at ~`main.rs:779`): call `adopt_view_state()`
  then `rebuild_items()` and `return true` to repaint now instead of waiting up to 1s. The
  acting instance's own broadcast no-ops via the seq guard.
- Fallback: if mode-narrowing proves flaky (see the digit-collision note at `main.rs:1868`),
  broadcast unnarrowed and let each instance's `adopt_view_state()` self-filter by its own
  `mode` file. The 1s timer is the correctness floor regardless; the pipe only reduces latency.

### Files / reuse
- `crates/panopt-zellij/src/main.rs` only. Touch points: `PanoptPane` fields (~440–553),
  `update()` (681), `pipe()` (743), `reload_data()` (1131), `clamp_cursor()` (1510),
  `request_focus_pane` emit pattern (1877), cockpit write/read helpers (~2589 / ~1375),
  `Mode::letter`/`slug`/`parse` (80–116).
- Reuse: atomic temp+rename write idiom, `parse_agent_labels`-style tolerant reader,
  `clamp_cursor`, existing `run_command` pipe emit.

## Invariants honored (CLAUDE.md)
- Atomic projection writes (temp+rename); writes only under `.cockpit/`, never `.panopt/*.md`.
- Plugin never closes panes — no pane-lifecycle calls added.
- One MCP tool surface — no new tool; `TOOL_SURFACE`/`Tool` enum untouched (plugin-internal).
- Dual-target build respected (WASM-only crate).

## Recommended first increment
Ship **cursor + scroll sync via the timer adopt path only (no pipe)**: add the fields,
`ViewState` (cursor/scroll/seq), `view_state_path`, `write_view_state`, `read_view_state`,
the Key/Mouse fingerprint-diff + `bump_and_persist_view`, and `adopt_view_state()` at the
end of `reload_data()`. Converges within ≤1s with zero pipe plumbing. Then add
filter/sort/show_help and the `panopt:view-sync` pipe for instant propagation.

Note: `show_help` is the one field safe to leave client-local if "identical" feels too
aggressive for a transient overlay — carry it in the struct regardless; dropping it from the
synced set is a one-field change.

## Out of scope (follow-up risk to track separately)
With a shared cursor, both clients' Todos "gatekeeper" instances drive content-pane
swaps/previews from the same cursor (`preview_cursor`, `main.rs:1558`), making simultaneous
slot swaps more likely. Not introduced by this change, but worth a separate todo: elect a
single gatekeeper client for swap/preview, or make `preview_cursor` idempotent against the
routing files it already writes (`write_routing`).

## Verification
1. Build: `cargo check --manifest-path crates/panopt-zellij/Cargo.toml --target wasm32-wasip1`,
   then `cargo clippy --manifest-path crates/panopt-zellij/Cargo.toml --target wasm32-wasip1 -- -D warnings`
   (or run the `verify-all` skill / `just clippy`). `just plugin-release` for the artifact;
   `just refresh` to reload the running cockpit.
2. `panopt up`, then attach a second client to the same Zellij session (`zellij attach <session>`
   from another terminal).
3. Move the cursor (`j`/`k`) in client A's Todos pane → client B's Todos cursor jumps to the
   same row within ≤1s (instantly if the pipe lands).
4. Press `f` (filter) and `1`/`2` (sort) in A → B's frame-title filter/sort label and list
   order match. Press `?` in A → B shows the help overlay (if `show_help` is synced).
5. Cross-mode isolation: move the cursor in A's Notes pane → B's Notes follows, neither
   client's Todos cursor moves.
6. Empty/short-list clamp: filter to a near-empty state in A → B clamps without a crashed or
   blank plugin pane.

{"started":true,"todo":{"assignee":"","blockers":[],"body":"
## Problem statement

Panopt works correctly in a single Zellij client, but when two clients attach to the same Zellij session, **plugin panes diverge between clients**.

Plain terminal panes behave as expected: both clients see the same PTY output. The divergence only happens in panes running a Panopt/Zellij plugin.

This indicates that the plugin’s visible state is being held inside a **client-local plugin instance**, rather than being derived from a **shared session-level state model**.

## Reproduction

1. Start Panopt in a named Zellij session.

   ```sh
   zellij attach --create panopt
   ```

2. From another terminal or machine, attach a second client to the same session.

   ```sh
   zellij attach panopt
   ```

3. In a normal terminal pane, type something.

   Expected: both clients see the same output.

4. In a Panopt plugin pane, change a visible value, mode, form field, selection, or pane content.

   Actual: the second client sees the change locally, but the first client does not.

## Expected behavior

All committed Panopt state should be shared across clients attached to the same Zellij session.

Examples of shared state:

```text
current view/mode
form field values
selected entity/task
pane role/assignment
command state
document/model contents
```

Client-local state is fine for transient UI details:

```text
cursor position
focus
scroll offset
selection
half-typed uncommitted input
hover/highlight state
```

## Likely root cause

Each attached Zellij client gets its own plugin instance or plugin render state. The plugin is treating its in-memory state as authoritative.

That works for one client, but fails with multiple attached clients because each plugin instance mutates only its own local state.

Current broken model:

```text
client A -> plugin instance A -> local state A
client B -> plugin instance B -> local state B
```

Needed model:

```text
client A -> plugin instance A ┐
```

## Problem statement

Panopt works correctly in a single Zellij client, but when two clients attach to the same Zellij session, **plugin panes diverge between clients**.

Plain terminal panes behave as expected: both clients see the same PTY output. The divergence only happens in panes running a Panopt/Zellij plugin.

This indicates that the plugin’s visible state is being held inside a **client-local plugin instance**, rather than being derived from a **shared session-level state model**.

## Reproduction

1. Start Panopt in a named Zellij session.

   ```sh
   zellij attach --create panopt
   ```

2. From another terminal or machine, attach a second client to the same session.

   ```sh
   zellij attach panopt
   ```

3. In a normal terminal pane, type something.

   Expected: both clients see the same output.

4. In a Panopt plugin pane, change a visible value, mode, form field, selection, or pane content.

   Actual: the second client sees the change locally, but the first client does not.

## Expected behavior

All committed Panopt state should be shared across clients attached to the same Zellij session.

Examples of shared state:

```text
current view/mode
form field values
selected entity/task
pane role/assignment
command state
document/model contents
```

Client-local state is fine for transient UI details:

```text
cursor position
focus
scroll offset
selection
half-typed uncommitted input
hover/highlight state
```

## Likely root cause

Each attached Zellij client gets its own plugin instance or plugin render state. The plugin is treating its in-memory state as authoritative.

That works for one client, but fails with multiple attached clients because each plugin instance mutates only its own local state.

Current broken model:

```text
client A -> plugin instance A -> local state A
client B -> plugin instance B -> local state B
```

Needed model:

```text
client A -> plugin instance A ┐
                              ├-> shared Panopt state -> broadcast/update -> all plugin instances repaint
client B -> plugin instance B ┘
```

Move authoritative Panopt state out of the plugin instance.

```text
single panoptd process per Zellij session
Unix socket
SQLite database
state file + file watcher
local event bus
Zellij plugin pipes, if suitable
```

On every committed change:

```text

state owner applies mutation

all plugin instances are notified or poll
all plugin instances reload state
all plugin panes repaint from the same snapshot
```

Implemented and verified to the extent this environment allows. Summary:

## What I did

Fixed the multiplayer divergence by externalizing the Zellij sidebar's **presentation state** to a shared, per-mode file that all clients' plugin instances read — so the sidebar now behaves like a shared terminal pane. All changes are in `crates/panopt-zellij/src/main.rs`.

**Root cause:** In Zellij multiplayer, each attached client runs its *own* plugin WASM instance with its own `thread_local` state. The list *data* already converged (every instance polls `.panopt/*.md`), but the *view* state (`cursor`, `scroll`, `todo_filter`, `todo_sort_1/2`, `show_help`) lived only in instance memory and never synced.

**The fix:**
- **Shared store** — `ViewState` written atomically (temp+rename) to `.cockpit/view-<letter>.json`, one file per mode (`Mode::letter`), with a monotonic `seq` for last-writer-wins. `TodoFilter`/`TodoSort` get stable `to_wire`/`from_wire` codes off the existing append-only `ALL_*` arrays.
- **Write-on-change** — in `update()`, the `Key`/`Mouse` arms snapshot a `view_fingerprint()` before/after the handler; on a real change, `bump_and_persist_view()` writes the file and broadcasts. Timer/PaneUpdate ticks deliberately don't write (they only re-clamp, identically on every client).
- **Read-and-adopt** — `adopt_view_state()` at the end of `reload_data()` adopts a strictly-newer `seq` (skips the instance's own write, never regresses). The existing `rebuild_items()`→`clamp_cursor()` that runs right after validates adopted cursor/scroll against the local list.
- **Instant propagation** — a `panopt:view-sync` pipe (broadcast unnarrowed, self-filtered by mode-slug payload, mirroring the `focus-pane` pattern) makes other clients repaint immediately rather than waiting up to 1s. The timer remains the correctness floor.

Added 3 unit tests (wire round-trips, field parser tolerance).

## Verification
- ✅ `clippy --target wasm32-wasip1 -- -D warnings` clean (incl. `--tests`)
- ✅ release WASM artifact builds clean; `fmt --check` clean
- ⚠️ Plugin unit tests can't *link* on host here — zellij-tile's host FFI symbols (`host_run_plugin_command`) are undefined off-wasm. This is a pre-existing environmental wall (blocks all this crate's host tests), not my change; compilation reaches the link stage, so the test code type-checks.
- ⏳ The two-client behavior needs a manual check: `just refresh`, attach two clients (`zellij attach <session>`), move the cursor / change filter-sort / press `?` in one → the other follows within ≤1s; confirm cross-mode isolation (Notes cursor doesn't move Todos).

## Notes
- I'm on branch `fix/116-multiplayer-view-sync`; todo #116 is locked by me and still `in_progress`. I haven't committed (will do so on your say-so) or marked it complete (pending the live two-client check).
- **Out of scope / follow-up:** with a now-shared cursor, both clients' Todos *gatekeeper* instances drive content-pane previews from the same cursor, making simultaneous slot swaps more likely. Worth a separate todo (elect one gatekeeper, or make `preview_cursor` idempotent) — say the word and I'll file it.

Want me to run `just refresh` so you can test it live, and/or commit?

content.text:
Root cause is now fully pinned down. Two independent walls, neither caused by your changes:

1. **Host build can't link** — the crate calls zellij-tile shims that import host functions (`host_run_plugin_command`, etc.) provided only by Zellij's WASM runtime. Off-wasm they're undefined symbols. The crate is **wasm-only by design**; `crates/panopt-zellij/.cargo/config.toml` pins `target = "wasm32-wasip1"` *but only when cargo's cwd is inside the crate*. My earlier `cargo test --manifest-path …` ran from the repo root, bypassed that config, built for host → the link error. That was my invocation mistake, not a regression.

2. **WASM build can't execute** — running from inside the crate builds correctly for wasm, but there's **no WASI runtime installed** (`wasmtime`/`wasmer`/`wasm3` all absent) and **no `runner` configured**, so cargo tries to exec the `.wasm` natively → `Exec format error`.

So in this environment the plugin's unit tests (mine *and* the pre-existing ones) can be **compiled/type-checked but never executed**. The build from inside the crate did compile my tests into the `.wasm` successfully — only execution is blocked.

Let me confirm the only missing piece is a runtime, and whether one is installable here:

Definitive root cause confirmed and airtight. The dump shows exactly one problematic import: `func[0] … <- zellij.host_run_plugin_command`. Everything else is standard `wasi_snapshot_preview1` (which wasmtime provides). That single `zellij.*` import is supplied **only by the real Zellij host**, so any generic runtime aborts at instantiation before a test runs.

So `cargo test` is **compile-only** for this crate by construction — host can't link the import, wasmtime can't instantiate it. This is true of the pre-existing tests too; it predates and is independent of my change.

One thing worth checking: modern wasmtime can trap (instead of reject) unknown imports, which would let the pure tests run since they never call that function. Let me see if this wasmtime supports it.

content.text:
Fully root-caused, and I actually ran the tests to prove it. Here's the chain:

## Why the tests "can't link" — the real story

It's **not** a regression from your changes (or mine). The crate's tests are **compile-only by construction** with stock tooling, for layered reasons:

1. **My first error was invocation.** I ran `cargo test --manifest-path … ` from the repo root. The crate's `crates/panopt-zellij/.cargo/config.toml` (`target = "wasm32-wasip1"`) is only honored when cargo's **cwd is inside the crate** — so my command built for the **host** target, where zellij-tile's host import `host_run_plugin_command` is an undefined symbol → the link error I mis-reported as "environmental."

2. **Run it correctly (from in-crate) and host isn't even the target** — it builds for wasm fine, but `cargo test` then can't execute the `.wasm`: no WASI runtime is installed and no `runner` is configured → `Exec format error`.

3. **Give it a real runtime (wasmtime) and it still won't run** — the wasm module imports `zellij.host_run_plugin_command` (confirmed in the import table: it's the one non-`wasi_snapshot_preview1` import). That function is supplied **only by the real Zellij host**, so wasmtime aborts at instantiation: `unknown import … has not been defined`.

4. **Tell wasmtime to trap unknown imports** (`-W unknown-imports-trap=y`) and the harness finally runs. The pure tests pass; only tests that genuinely call host functions (e.g. the pre-existing `ingest_panes_captures_each_viewer_slot_name`) trap.

So: the plugin compiles to one wasm module that links Zellij host imports into the *test* binary, and neither the host linker nor a generic wasm runtime can satisfy them — only Zellij can. Plain `cargo test` has therefore never executed this crate's tests; they've only ever been *type-checked* by compilation. That's pre-existing.

**Proof my new tests are sound** — run under the trap-imports runner:
```
cargo test wire        → 2 passed   (todo_filter / todo_sort wire round-trips)
cargo test view_field  → 1 passed   (field parser)
```

## Options to make them actually runnable
- **A (quick, ~2 lines):** add to `crates/panopt-zellij/.cargo/config.toml`:
  `[target.wasm32-wasip1]` / `runner = "wasmtime run -W unknown-imports-trap=y"`. Then `cargo test` (run *in-crate*) executes all the pure tests; host-touching ones must be name-filtered. Requires `wasmtime` on PATH.
- **B (cleanest, a refactor):** move the pure logic (parsers, the new wire/`view_field` helpers, `classify_pane`, etc.) into a small host-buildable lib crate with no `zellij-tile` dep — then `cargo test --workspace` runs them natively everywhere, no wasm runtime needed.
- **C:** a custom wasmtime harness that stubs `zellij::*` as no-ops, to run the *whole* suite including host-touching tests.

I'd suggest **A** now (cheap unblock) and **B** later if you want these in the normal `just test` workspace sweep. Want me to wire up A, or sketch B?

1	//! PANopt coordination sidebar - a Zellij plugin.
2	//!
3	//! Each plugin pane renders one kind of resource - todos, agents, terminals,
4	//! commands, or notes - selected by the `mode` value in its layout
5	//! config. The five panes stack vertically in the cockpit's left column, each
6	//! pinned to its own fixed proportion so adding or removing panes on the
7	//! right cannot reshape any of them. A keyboard cursor walks the pane's items
8	//! and scrolls when it hits the visible window's edge; the mouse clicks any
9	//! row.
10	//!
11	//! The cockpit is these five panes plus one content pane on the right.
12	//! Selecting an item swaps its pane into that one slot and suppresses
13	//! whatever was there - a suppressed pane keeps running, just hidden, no
14	//! stack and no title bar. Documents (todos, notes, lists) all share
15	//! one re-pointable `panopt _viewer` pane; agents, commands, and terminals
16	//! are each their own pane. Moving the cursor previews the selected item in
17	//! the slot - or clears the slot when the row has nothing to show - always
18	//! without taking focus off the plugin pane. A click does the same; Enter
19	//! additionally focuses the pane.
20	//!
21	//! If the user splits the content pane, a selection swaps into whichever
22	//! pane was focused last before any plugin pane took focus - the designated
23	//! slot. Each of the five panes derives the slot independently from the same
24	//! `PaneUpdate` manifest, so they all converge on the same target.
25	//!
26	//! The Todos plugin pane doubles as the cockpit gatekeeper: it is the only
27	//! pane that handles the close-request and spawn pipes (see `up::render_config`).
28	//! When an active agent, command, or terminal would be lost, the Todos pane
29	//! refuses by showing a floating dialog with a `close anyway` override; any
30	//! of the five plugin panes themselves cannot be closed.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import re, sys

MAIN = "crates/panopt-zellij/src/main.rs"
LIB = "crates/panopt-zellij-logic/src/lib.rs"

with open(MAIN) as f:
    lines = f.readlines()  # 0-indexed; line N (1-indexed) = lines[N-1]

n = len(lines)

def brace_end(start0):
    """Given 0-indexed start line of an item, return 0-indexed end line (the
    line where braces balance back to 0)."""
    depth = 0
    seen = False
    i = start0
    while i < n:
        for ch in lines[i]:
            if ch == '{':
                depth += 1; seen = True
            elif ch == '}':
                depth -= 1
        if seen and depth == 0:
            return i
        i += 1
    raise RuntimeError(f"unbalanced from line {start0+1}")

def with_doc(start0):
    """Walk upward including contiguous ///, //!, and #[...] attribute lines."""
    j = start0
    while j-1 >= 0:
        s = lines[j-1].lstrip()
        if s.startswith('///') or s.startswith('#['):
            j -= 1
        else:
            break
    return j

# --- code blocks ---
EXPLICIT = [(63, 412)]  # 1-indexed inclusive: Mode + TodoFilter + parsers + TodoSort
ANCHORS = [
    "struct ProcessRow {",
    "enum PaneRole {",
    "fn is_user_shell(",
    "fn classify_pane(",
    "struct ViewState {",
    "fn view_field(",
    "fn parse_agent_labels(",
    "fn split_top_level(",
    "fn parse_viewer_slot(",
    "fn parse_viewer_routing(",
    "fn viewer_title_for(",
    "fn lookup_title(",
    "fn kind_prefixed_title(",
    "fn parse_index_line(",
    "fn parse_process_line(",
]

code_ranges = []  # (start0, end0)
for (a, b) in EXPLICIT:
    code_ranges.append((a-1, b-1))

for anc in ANCHORS:
    found = None
    for i in range(n):
        if lines[i].startswith(anc):
            found = i; break
    if found is None:
        raise RuntimeError(f"anchor not found: {anc}")
    end0 = brace_end(found)
    start0 = with_doc(found)
    code_ranges.append((start0, end0))

# --- test functions ---
TEST_NAMES = [
 "parses_a_todo_index_line","parse_priority_suffix_skips_the_trailing_updated_token",
 "parse_updated_suffix_extracts_the_timestamp","parse_updated_suffix_returns_none_when_absent",
 "modified_desc_sorts_by_timestamp_not_id","parses_a_note_index_line",
 "parses_a_note_index_line_with_updated_timestamp","ignores_non_index_lines",
 "empty_title_note_line_keeps_the_suffix_in_the_label",
 "empty_title_todo_line_still_parses_status_and_priority",
 "suffix_start_picks_the_right_marker_for_each_shape","parses_a_process_line",
 "parses_a_process_line_with_a_from_suffix","ignores_non_process_lines",
 "classify_pane_reads_the_launch_command","parse_viewer_routing_reads_kind_and_id",
 "parse_viewer_routing_tolerates_garbage","viewer_title_for_each_known_kind",
 "kind_prefixed_title_avoids_doubling_the_kind_word","mode_hotkey_mapping_is_consistent",
 "parse_viewer_slot_extracts_the_slot_token","agent_labels_parser_tolerates_malformed_input",
 "todo_filter_wire_codes_round_trip","todo_sort_wire_codes_round_trip",
 "view_field_reads_each_key_and_tolerates_absence",
]

test_ranges = []
for name in TEST_NAMES:
    pat = re.compile(r'^\s*fn '+re.escape(name)+r'\b')
    found = None
    for i in range(n):
        if pat.match(lines[i]):
            found = i; break
    if found is None:
        raise RuntimeError(f"test fn not found: {name}")
    end0 = brace_end(found)
    start0 = with_doc(found)  # includes #[test] and any /// above
    test_ranges.append((start0, end0))

# --- build moved-line set & ordered chunk text ---
def chunk_text(ranges):
    ranges = sorted(ranges)
    return ["".join(lines[a:b+1]) for (a, b) in ranges]

moved = set()
for (a, b) in code_ranges + test_ranges:
    for k in range(a, b+1):
        if k in moved:
            raise RuntimeError(f"overlap at line {k+1}")
        moved.add(k)

code_text = "\n".join(chunk_text(code_ranges))
test_text = "\n".join(chunk_text(test_ranges))

# --- pub transformation on code ---
def pub_code(text):
    out = []
    in_struct = False
    for ln in text.split("\n"):
        raw = ln
        if raw.startswith("struct "):
            raw = "pub " + raw; in_struct = True
        elif raw.startswith("enum "):
            raw = "pub " + raw
        elif raw.startswith("fn "):
            raw = "pub " + raw
        elif raw.startswith("const "):
            raw = "pub " + raw
        elif raw.startswith("    fn "):
            raw = "    pub " + raw[4:]
        elif in_struct and re.match(r'^    [a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*: ', raw):
            raw = "    pub " + raw[4:]
        if raw.startswith("}"):

        out.append(raw)
    return "\n".join(out)

code_text = pub_code(code_text)

"//! panopt_zellij_logic::*` and adds the Zellij-bound view/controller on top.\n"
"\n"
"use std::cmp::Ordering;\n"
"\n"
)

with open(LIB, "w") as f:
    f.write(LIB_HEADER)
    f.write(code_text)
    if not code_text.endswith("\n"):
        f.write("\n")
    f.write("\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n")
    f.write(test_text)
    f.write("}\n")

# --- rewrite main.rs: drop moved lines, insert glob use after line 36 ---
new = []
for idx in range(n):
    if idx in moved:
        continue
    new.append(lines[idx])
    if idx == 35:  # 0-indexed line 36 = `use zellij_tile::prelude::*;`
        new.append("\n")
        new.append("use panopt_zellij_logic::*;\n")

with open(MAIN, "w") as f:
    f.writelines(new)

print(f"moved {len(code_ranges)} code blocks, {len(test_ranges)} tests, {len(moved)} lines")
print("code ranges (1-indexed):", sorted([(a+1,b+1) for a,b in code_ranges]))

Done. Option B is implemented and fully verified.

## What changed

Extracted the plugin's **transport-free logic** into a new host-buildable workspace crate, `panopt-zellij-logic`, so its unit tests run in the normal `cargo test --workspace` sweep — no WASM runtime, no Zellij host needed.

**New crate `crates/panopt-zellij-logic`** (`src/lib.rs`) now owns the pure pieces: the `Mode`/`TodoFilter`/`TodoSort` enums + methods (incl. the `to_wire`/`from_wire` codes), `ProcessRow`/`PaneRole`/`ViewState`, all the projection-line parsers (`parse_index_line`, `parse_process_line`, `suffix_start`, `parse_*_suffix`, `classify_pane`, `parse_viewer_*`, `viewer_title_for`, `lookup_title`, `kind_prefixed_title`, `parse_agent_labels`, `split_top_level`), and `view_field` — **plus the 26 unit tests** that exercise them.

**The plugin (`panopt-zellij`)** keeps everything Zellij-bound (`PanoptPane`, `PaneRow`, `Item`, `ItemTarget`, all the `fs`/host functions and their `PaneInfo`/`PaneManifest` tests), depends on the new crate by path, and re-exports it with `use panopt_zellij_logic::*;` so no call sites changed.

## Why this is the right fix
The plugin compiles to one WASM module that imports `zellij.host_run_plugin_command`; that import is linked into the *test* binary too, so neither the host linker nor a generic WASM runtime could ever run `cargo test` there. Moving the pure code to a crate with no `zellij-tile` dependency sidesteps the host ABI entirely — that code builds and tests like any other workspace crate, on host *and* wasm.

## Verification
- `cargo test --workspace` → **26** logic tests run natively and pass, alongside the existing 147 + 100 + 2 + 5 (all green).
- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo clippy --manifest-path crates/panopt-zellij/Cargo.toml --target wasm32-wasip1 --tests -- -D warnings` clean (plugin's remaining tests still compile via the glob re-export).
- Release WASM artifact builds; `cargo fmt --check` clean on both crates.
- Temp extraction script removed.

The `#116` multiplayer view-sync work from before is unchanged and rides on top; its `to_wire`/`from_wire`/`view_field` tests are now among the 26 that run in CI-style `cargo test`.

content.text:
Decisive detail: `PipeSource::Keybind` carries **no** client info (the enum literally has a `TODO` about it). So a gatekeeper can't tell from the pipe which client pressed `alt-n` — both `mode=todos` instances get an identical message. The fix must be **gatekeeper election**: exactly one Todos instance (across clients) acts on the cockpit-wide mutating pipes.

The cleanest election key is "I belong to the lowest-numbered connected client" — Zellij tracks the client list authoritatively, so leadership transfers automatically when a client detaches, with no file/heartbeat/wall-clock. Let me verify the API supports it (`list_clients` + a result event with client ids, and `get_plugin_ids().client_id`).

content.text:
Fixed. Implemented **gatekeeper election** so the spawn pipes act exactly once across clients.

## Root cause
`Alt-n` is a Zellij keybind that runs `zellij action pipe --name panopt:spawn-blank-pane --plugin-configuration mode=todos`. With two clients attached there are **two** `mode=todos` gatekeeper instances (one per client), and the pipe broadcasts to **both** → both spawn. And `PipeSource::Keybind` carries no client identity (the zellij-utils enum has a literal `TODO` about it), so a gatekeeper can't tell from the pipe which client pressed the key. This is **pre-existing multiplayer behavior** — my view-sync change doesn't touch spawn pipes; it just made multiplayer usable enough to surface it.
- *Both on the right → two panes*: both gatekeepers spawn.
- *One in sidebar, one on right → appears then vanishes*: both spawn, then the sidebar-focused client's gatekeeper runs its slot logic and **suppresses** (hides) the pane the other just made.

## The fix
Elect a single leader: the Todos instance whose client is the **lowest-numbered connected client**, computed from Zellij's `Event::ListClients` (`ClientInfo { client_id, is_current_client }`). Only the leader acts on `panopt:spawn-agent` / `panopt:spawn-blank-pane`. Client ids are monotonic per attach, so the first client leads and stays leading; when its client detaches, leadership deterministically falls to the next-lowest within one 1s poll — no files, heartbeats, or wall-clock. Defaults to leader=true so a lone client spawns immediately before the first client list arrives.

In `crates/panopt-zellij/src/main.rs`: new `is_gatekeeper_leader` field, subscribe to `ListClients` + request it in `load()` and each timer tick (Todos only), `update_gatekeeper_leadership()`, and a leader-guard on the two spawn arms.

## Verified
- Plugin wasm clippy + `--tests` clean (`-D warnings`); release artifact builds; fmt clean.
- `cargo test --workspace` still green (26 logic tests + the rest).
- Behavioral check needs two live clients — that's yours to run.

## Two things for you
1. **Same latent bug in the other gatekeeper pipes** — I gated *only* spawn (your report). `close-focus-request` / `close-tab-request` / `quit-request` / the gate-decision pipes / `open-search` also broadcast to both gatekeepers and will double-fire (two close-dialogs, etc.). I held off because their dialogs appear on a *specific* client and gating to the leader would pop the dialog on the wrong screen — that needs a per-acting-client routing answer the pipe can't currently give. Want me to extend election to them anyway (accepting the dialog-on-leader wrinkle), or leave them?
2. To test live, the cockpit needs the rebuilt plugin — `just refresh` reloads it (it tears down the session's panes, so I didn't run it unprompted). Want me to?

Confirmed the critical fact: `focus_pane_with_id` (and all focus APIs) act only on **the plugin's own client** — there's no all-clients focus. But `PaneId` is **session-global**, so focus-sync works exactly like the view-sync I already built: broadcast the focused pane id, and every other client's instance calls `focus_pane_with_id` to match (with a seq guard against feedback).

## Why this is the right direction
Focus-sync makes the cockpit a **single mirrored viewport** — which is what "identical/synchronized" means and what panopt's design already assumes. Once focus is shared:
- The focus-keyed **spawn gate decides identically** on every gatekeeper (no more "one refuses, one spawns").
- The **single content slot** becomes coherent (all clients derive the same `slot_pane`).
- **Election becomes correct.** It only broke before because the leader executed in *its own* divergent focus context. With focus synced, the leader's context *is* everyone's context — so "one elected gatekeeper does the spawn/gate work" is now sound.

## The plan (two parts, both reusing the view-sync machinery)
1. **Sync focus**: when a client's focus changes to a non-transient pane (ignore the `is_transient_pipe_pane` flicker that already exists), broadcast its `PaneId`; each other instance self-applies `focus_pane_with_id`, guarded by a seq like `view_seq` so it doesn't echo.
2. **Re-introduce election** (the revert-of-the-revert), now valid: the lowest-client gatekeeper alone runs spawn/gate work; everyone sees the right result because focus+view are mirrored.

## Honest caveats
- **Behavioral change**: clients navigate *together* — one person moving focus moves everyone's. That's inherent to "identical." If you ever want independent navigation, this is the wrong model and we'd need per-client slots instead.
- **Risks to handle carefully**: focus feedback loops (seq guard), the transient pipe-pane focus theft (existing filter covers it), and keeping input-mode (Locked/Normal) consistent with the shared focus. Focus-sync is more intrusive than view-sync, so it's worth doing in a small, testable increment.

content.text:
Focus-sync (first increment) is implemented and builds/tests clean. It mirrors **content-pane focus** across clients, Todos-gatekeeper-only, using the same seq-guarded `.cockpit` file + pipe pattern as view-sync.

## What it does
When a client focuses a content (right-side) pane — clicking into it, or `Enter` on a sidebar item — the Todos gatekeeper publishes that pane to `.cockpit/focus.json` and broadcasts `panopt:focus-sync`; every other client's gatekeeper focuses the same pane (instantly via the pipe, ≤1s via the timer fallback). So the right-side viewport mirrors across clients.

## Deliberate scope/limits of this increment
- **Content (terminal) focus only.** Terminal pane ids are session-global, so they're portable. Sidebar plugin-pane ids differ per client, so sidebar focus is *not* mirrored yet — focusing the sidebar leaves peers on the last content pane rather than yanking them.
- **No election yet.** Spawn duplication (`alt-n` → two panes) is *still present* — that's intentional. Per your plan, confirm mirroring is clean first, then I re-add election (which becomes correct once focus is shared).
- **Guarded against the split bug** (commit 669c107): a peer only adopts focus to a pane that's visible locally, never a suppressed one, so it can't resurface-and-split.

## What to look for with two clients
- Click into / `Enter` a content pane on client A → client B's focus follows to the same pane within ≤1s.
- Move A's focus to the sidebar → B stays put (not yanked).
- No focus ping-pong, no panes splitting.

Verified: wasm clippy + `--tests` clean (`-D warnings`), release builds, `cargo test --workspace` green.

To test live the cockpit needs the rebuilt plugin — `just refresh` reloads it (tears down the session's panes, so I didn't run it unprompted). Want me to run it, or will you?

1. **`is_focused` in the manifest is effectively global/shared, not per-client.** Both per-client instances report the *same* focused pane. So the plugin **cannot observe each client's individual focus** through `PaneUpdate` — which is the only channel it has. Plugin-driven focus mirroring is therefore not achievable this way; there's no per-client focus signal to read or broadcast.

2. **Content panes barely hold focus in the cockpit at all** — every reading is a plugin/sidebar pane (`p1`, `p3`), never a terminal. The cockpit's own focus management keeps focus on the sidebar (preview returns focus to the plugin pane), so `focused_non_plugin` is almost always `None` — which is why only one `PUB` (`t0`) ever fired and `focus.json` is frozen at `seq=1`.

So both the election attempt and this focus-sync attempt were built on a model — independent, plugin-observable per-client focus — that **doesn't hold in this Zellij setup**. The data also suggests Zellij is already treating focus as largely session-global, which means there may be little for the plugin to "mirror" in the first place.

**My recommendation:** stop the speculative focus/spawn patching on your live session. Revert the focus-sync experiment **and** all the debug instrumentation, keeping the two pieces that are sound and independently valuable:
- **view-sync** (sidebar list/cursor mirroring — the thing that "mostly works"),
- **the host-testable `panopt-zellij-logic` crate** (26 tests now run in `cargo test --workspace`).

Then treat multiplayer content/focus/spawn as a separate, deliberate investigation into Zellij's actual multiplayer focus/render model (quite possibly an upstream behavior question), rather than more guesses.

    #!/usr/bin/env bash

        zellij delete-session "$s" 2>/dev/null || true

    pkill -TERM -x panoptd 2>/dev/null || true
    sleep 1
    pkill -TERM -x panoptd 2>/dev/null || true

This is the real fix: it's a session-level Zellij setting, not plugin gymnastics. If it works, then **all** my plugin-side sync experiments (view-sync, focus-sync, the election, and the debug instrumentation) become unnecessary and I'll rip them out — leaving just this one config line plus the host-testable crate refactor. Tell me how the test goes and I'll do that cleanup.

---
name: project_zellij_multiplayer_mirror
description: panopt multiplayer mirroring relies on Zellij mirror_session; plugin-level focus/view sync is a dead end
metadata:
  type: project
---

panopt's cockpit must look the same on every attached client (tmux-style). The
ONLY thing that achieves this is Zellij's session option **`mirror_session true`**,
injected into the generated cockpit config by `ensure_mirror_session_enabled` in
`crates/panopt/src/up.rs`. Zellij's default multiplayer is *independent* per-client
viewports (separate focus/cursor, like collaborative editing), NOT a shared viewport.

**Why plugin-level sync cannot work (verified the hard way, May 2026):**
- A Zellij plugin pane is a separate WASM instance *per client* (distinguish by
  `get_plugin_ids().client_id` — NOT `plugin_id`, which is keyed to the layout pane
  and identical across clients).
- The `PaneManifest`/`is_focused` a plugin receives is effectively **global**, not
  per-client: both clients' instances report the same focused pane. So a plugin
  **cannot observe each client's individual focus**, which makes plugin-driven
  focus/view mirroring (broadcast-a-file-+-adopt) impossible.
- `PipeSource::Keybind`/`Cli` carry no client id, so a broadcast pipe (e.g. the
  `Alt-n` spawn) can't tell which client triggered it — gatekeeper "election" by
  lowest client also fails because each gatekeeper runs in its own focus context.

**Gotcha that bit us:** the stock Zellij config ships a *commented* `// mirror_session true`
doc line. A naive `config.contains("mirror_session true")` matches the comment and
skips injecting a real directive — the session launches unmirrored. The fix must be
comment-aware (ignore lines whose first non-space token is `//`). See
[[feedback_rebuild_runtime_artifacts]] — `mirror_session` only applies at session
creation, so `just refresh` (full teardown + recreate) is required, not a plugin reload.

Done. The fix landed and the experiments are cleaned up.

## Outcome

The real fix for #116 is one Zellij session option — **`mirror_session true`** — which gives the tmux-style mirroring you wanted: every attached client shares one viewport (same focus, same panes, same everything), including the spawn behavior. It's injected into panopt's generated cockpit config by a new comment-aware `ensure_mirror_session_enabled` in `crates/panopt/src/up.rs`.

### What this took, and the lesson
Zellij's *default* multiplayer is independent per-client viewports (collaborative-editing style), not a shared one. I burned several rounds trying to mirror it from inside the plugin (view-sync, focus-sync, gatekeeper election) before the instrumentation proved why that's impossible: **a plugin can't observe per-client focus** — the manifest's `is_focused` is global, and pipes don't carry the originating client. So no plugin-level scheme can work; it had to be the session-level setting. (Saved to memory so this isn't re-discovered the hard way.)

The one bug that made `mirror_session` look like it failed was mine: Zellij ships a *commented* `// mirror_session true` doc line, and my first cut matched that substring and skipped injecting a real directive. Now comment-aware, with a test for exactly that case.

### Final state of the branch (`fix/116-multiplayer-view-sync`)
**Kept (two sound pieces):**
- `mirror_session true` config injection — the actual fix (4 tests).
- New **`panopt-zellij-logic`** crate — the plugin's pure parsers/enums extracted so they finally run under `cargo test --workspace` (23 tests; previously unrunnable because the plugin links Zellij's host ABI).

**Removed (all the dead ends):** view-sync, focus-sync, election, and the debug instrumentation — plus the on-disk `.cockpit` artifacts they wrote. Net `main.rs`: −926 lines.

**Verified:** `cargo test --workspace` green, plugin wasm clippy + `--tests` clean (`-D warnings`), release wasm builds, fmt clean. I also reverted three files that `cargo fmt -p panopt` had incidentally reformatted, so the diff stays focused.

Still on the branch, nothing committed, todo #116 still `in_progress` under my lock. Want me to commit, and/or mark #116 complete? (Note the branch name `fix/116-multiplayer-view-sync` is now a bit of a misnomer — happy to rename it to something like `fix/116-mirror-session` if you'd like.)


panes, and spawns a first Claude agent already wired in. Re-running
`panopt up` later just re-attaches.

Focus a sidebar pane to drive it; each pane shows its own key hints in
the status bar.

## Driving PANopt from the shell

The `panopt` CLI can do everything the cockpit does, so you can script it
or work outside the cockpit entirely:

```sh
panopt todo list
panopt todo create "wire the form"
panopt todo set 3 --status in_progress --priority high --assignee alice
panopt todo done 3
panopt todo block 4 --by 3
panopt todo comment 3 "started" --as greg

panopt agent                # spawn another agent pane in the cockpit
panopt agent-tool list      # configured agent commands
panopt process list         # everything the cockpit is running
```

Each invocation targets the current project (override with `--ws <path>`)
and auto-starts the daemon if needed.

## Connecting agents you launched yourself

`panopt up` wires up the agents it spawns automatically. For an agent you
already started by hand - or one on another machine - use `panopt
agent-config` to print the connection details and pass them straight to
your agent CLI:

```sh
claude --mcp-config "$(panopt agent-config --name my-name)"
```

That session shows up in the agents list as `my-name` and shares the same
todos, notes, and locks as the cockpit-spawned agents.

### From another machine

Run the daemon on one host (your workstation, a NAS) and an agent on
another (a Mac, a laptop, a host with USB debug hardware). The agent host
only needs the `panopt` binary and your agent CLI.

On the daemon host, bind to the LAN and print the token:

```sh
panopt up --host 0.0.0.0
panopt token
```

On the agent host, hand the token to your agent:

```sh
TOKEN=$(ssh workstation panopt token)
claude --mcp-config "$(panopt agent-config \
    --host workstation.local \
    --token $TOKEN \
    --name solo-mac)"
```

**Security note:** the daemon speaks plain HTTP, so the token travels in
cleartext. Fine on a trusted LAN; tunnel through SSH (`ssh -L
7600:localhost:7600 workstation` and use `--host 127.0.0.1`) or WireGuard
for anything less trusted.

[DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) is the full design document - architecture, the MCP
tool reference, why PANopt is shaped the way it is. Read it if you want

## Sharing a cockpit

A cockpit is a single shared view, so more than one person can sit in it
at once. Open another terminal on the same machine (or SSH into it) and
either re-run `panopt up` in the same project, or attach to the cockpit's
Zellij session directly:

```sh
zellij attach            # pick the cockpit's session from the list
```

Every attached terminal sees the **same** screen, mirrored live - the same
sidebar selection, the same focused pane, the same content - the way `tmux`
mirrors a session. Move the cursor, switch panes, or open a viewer on one,
and it updates on all of them. That makes pairing and over-the-shoulder
review work without anyone's view drifting out of sync.

(PANopt turns on Zellij's `mirror_session` in the cockpit config to make
this work. Stock Zellij instead gives each client an independent cursor and
focus, which leaves the sidebar panes showing different things on each
screen.)
